gaps.sentence: How ___ people came to the meeting?
gaps.explanation: 'Many' is used with countable plural nouns like people; 'much' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ than twenty people at the meeting.
___ of the three routes avoids the toll entirely.
gaps.hint: not any of three or more
gaps.explanation: 'None of' is used for three or more; 'neither' only for two.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: We haven't got ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough chairs' means a sufficient number; 'too' before the noun would give the wrong meaning and position.
'Some' is used in offers and requests where we expect agreement; 'any' is for neutral questions.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: There are ___ than forty applicants for every training place.
gaps.explanation: 'More than' + number expresses quantities above a figure.
